extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic geometry (Math 216); advanced undergraduates / beginning graduate students
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of definitions and verifiable criteria for geometric properties (smoothness, separatedness, properness, regularity), the Artin–Rees/Krull intersection results, and foundational definitions/properties of vector bundles and locally free / invertible sheaves. Suitable for checking or proving these properties on schemes and sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: smooth over a ring A = smooth over Spec A
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase “smooth over a ring A” is interpreted to mean “smooth over Spec A”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a notational convention used throughout: checking smoothness over a ring is checking smoothness of the structure morphism to Spec A.

rubrics_metrics.name: k-smooth (smooth over Spec k) of relative dimension n (Jacobian/corank condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: X is smooth of relative dimension n over Spec k if locally X is an open subset W ⊂ Spec k[x1,...,xn+r]/(f1,...,fr) as in Definition 12.6.2, and the Jacobian matrix of the fi with respect to the xi has corank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, at closed points the Zariski tangent space is cut out by the Jacobian matrix and has dimension n; this yields that X has pure dimension n. The Jacobian corank hypothesis is the local computational test for k-smoothness used in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: pure dimension preserved under base change to k (Exercise 11.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a scheme X of finite type over k, X_k := X ⊗_k k̄ is pure dimension n iff X is pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows checking pure dimensionality after extension of the base field; used when relating tangent space dimension to scheme dimension via base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski tangent space cut out by Jacobian (Exercise 12.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zariski tangent space at a closed point of a finite type k-scheme is cut out by the Jacobian matrix of local defining equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the bridge from the algebraic Jacobian/corank condition to geometric tangent-space dimension bounds (Theorem 12.2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull Principal Ideal Theorem as dimension lower bound (Theorem 11.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a closed point p of a finite type scheme, Krull’s Principal Ideal Theorem implies the scheme has dimension at least the expected number (used to show dim X_k ≥ n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with tangent-space upper bound from Jacobian to deduce equality of dimension when corank hypothesis holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for separatedness (DVR version, Theorem 12.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y of finite type between locally Noetherian schemes, π is separated iff for every discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K(A) and every commutative diagram Spec K(A) → X over Spec A → Y (i.e., a map from the generic point), there is at most one morphism Spec A → X making the diagram commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to check separatedness by testing uniqueness of extensions of maps from punctured DVRs. Intuition: Spec A is a 'germ of a curve'; separatedness means unique extension of a punctured family if it extends at all. One direction (separated ⇒ valuative property) is straightforward via the Reduced-to-Separated Theorem 10.2.2 (Exercise 12.7.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for separatedness (general valuation rings, Theorem 12.7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is quasiseparated, then π is separated iff for any valuation ring A with fraction field K and any diagram Spec K → X over Spec A → Y there is at most one morphism Spec A → X filling the diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the DVR version to arbitrary valuation rings; proofs and references are given (Stacks, EGA). Typically used whenever valuation rings naturally arise (e.g., moduli problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for universal closedness and properness (DVR version, Theorem 12.7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y of finite type of locally Noetherian schemes and any DVR A with fraction field K, π is universally closed (resp. proper) iff for every diagram Spec K → X over Spec A → Y there is at least one (resp. exactly one) morphism Spec A → X making the diagram commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets universal closedness as existence of extensions, and properness as existence and uniqueness. Useful intuition: properness = limits of one-parameter families exist and are unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for universal closedness and properness (general, Theorem 12.7.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is quasiseparated and finite type, then π is universally closed (resp. proper) iff for any valuation ring A and any diagram Spec K → X over Spec A → Y there is at least one (resp. exactly one) morphism Spec A → X lifting the diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same as DVR version but for general valuation rings. Proof references: Stacks, EGA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of valuative criteria in moduli interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: When X is a fine moduli space over a field k, separatedness/properness of X has moduli-theoretic meaning: given a family over a punctured valuation ring, there is at most one (separated) / exactly one (proper) way to fill in the family over the closed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives geometric intuition for checking these properties in moduli problems (Remark 12.7.2, 12.7.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global test for regularity via closed points (Fact 12.8.2 consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian, to check Spec A is regular it suffices to check regularity at closed points (maximal ideals); localizations of regular local rings at primes are regular (Fact 12.8.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence for Noetherian schemes regularity can be checked at closed points (using Exercise 5.1.E and Fact 12.8.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity for finite type schemes over perfect fields (Theorem 12.8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is finite type over a perfect field k and regular at its closed points, then X is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a useful criterion for regularity in geometric situations over perfect fields; more general localizations of finite type algebras over perfect fields satisfy Fact 12.8.2 (Exercise 21.3.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are UFDs (Auslander–Buchsbaum Fact 12.8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is a regular local ring then A is a unique factorization domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a deep theorem (reference: [E], [Mat2]); consequence: regular schemes are factorial and hence normal (Exercise 5.4.F). The text notes this is not proved here but is a standard fact to use when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are integrally closed and Cohen–Macaulay
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular local rings are integrally closed (12.8.7) and Cohen–Macaulay (12.8.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrally closed follows from factoriality (Exercise 5.4.F) or will be proved in geometric cases later; Cohen–Macaulayness will be addressed in Chapter 26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: finite generation of Rees module ⇔ I-stability of filtration (Proposition 12.9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian and M a finitely generated A-module; for an I-filtration M = M0 ⊃ M1 ⊃ ... the graded module M•(I) := ⊕_{n≥0} Mn is finitely generated over the Rees algebra A•(I) := ⊕_{n≥0} I^n iff the filtration is I-stable (i.e., ∃ s s.t. I^d M_s = M_{d+s} for all d≥0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an algebraic criterion to detect when a filtration eventually behaves like the I-adic filtration; proofs hinge on Noetherianness of A•(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees Lemma (12.9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian, M a finitely generated A-module and (Mn) an I-stable filtration, and L ⊂ M a submodule, then the induced filtration L_n := L ∩ M_n is I-stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important technical lemma for controlling intersections of submodules with filtrations; used to prove corollaries like Corollary 12.9.4 and Krull intersection results. The proof uses finite generation of graded modules over Noetherian Rees algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees corollary (12.9.4) — eventual containment statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is an ideal of Noetherian A, M a finitely generated module, and L ⊂ M a submodule, then there exists s such that I^d (L ∩ I^s M) ⊂ I^{d+s} M for all d ≥ 0 (equivalently stated in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning in the text: it need not be true that I^d L = L ∩ I^d M. This corollary is an important application of Artin–Rees for controlling how submodules meet powers of an ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull Intersection Theorem (Exercise 12.9.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian and M finitely generated, with I a proper ideal, the intersection ∩_{j≥1} I^j M is zero under the stated hypotheses (exercise gives approach via Artin–Rees and Nakayama lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the algebraic statement that functions analytic-zero at a point vanish in a neighborhood in geometric contexts (connects to Exercise 12.9.B and Proposition 12.5.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a rank n vector bundle (13.1.0.1) and trivializations
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank n vector bundle π: V → M is a family of n-dimensional vector spaces parametrized by M such that for each x ∈ M there is a neighborhood U and a homeomorphism φ: π^{-1}(U) ≅ U × R^n commuting with projections and restricting to vector-space isomorphisms on fibers; such a φ is a trivialization over U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the topological/analytic definition; algebraic/scheme version is through locally free sheaves. Transition functions between trivializations lie in GL_n and must satisfy the cocycle condition (13.1.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition functions and cocycle condition (13.1.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given trivializations over open cover {U_i}, transition matrices T_{ij} ∈ GL_n(O(U_i ∩ U_j)) must satisfy T_{jk} ◦ T_{ij} = T_{ik} on triple overlaps (cocycle condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data (cover + transition functions) satisfying the cocycle condition uniquely determine the vector bundle (up to unique isomorphism) by gluing; conversely any vector bundle gives such data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaf definition and equivalence with vector bundles (13.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf of rank n on a scheme X is an O_X-module F such that there is an open cover {U_i} with F|_{U_i} ≅ O_{U_i}^{⊕n}. This is equivalent to the notion of a rank n vector bundle (sheaf of sections viewpoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the sheaf perspective for many algebraic constructions; trivializations produce transition functions for the sheaf just as for bundles. The sheaf definition is often shorter to state and more flexible on schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf-of-sections behavior under trivializations (13.1.2–13.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over a trivializing neighborhood U the sections of a rank n vector bundle correspond to n-tuples of functions; on overlaps these n-tuples are related by the transition matrices T_{ij} via T_{ij}⃗s_i = ⃗s_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the concrete method for describing sections and checking glueing conditions; helpful to compute local equations of subschemes cut out by sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible sheaf / line bundle and Picard group (13.1.4, 13.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank 1 locally free sheaf is called an invertible sheaf (line bundle). Invertible sheaves up to isomorphism form an abelian group under tensor product, called Pic X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invertible sheaves are the 'units' for tensor product of O_X-modules; Picard group methods classify line bundles, and Pic is a contravariant functor under pullback (Exercise 13.1.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations on locally free sheaves: duals, tensor, Hom, exactness (Exercises 13.1.B–13.1.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are locally free of ranks m,n then Hom(F,G) is locally free of rank mn. The dual E^∨ := Hom(E,O_X) of a rank n locally free E is locally free of rank n and E ≅ E^{∨∨}. Tensoring by a locally free sheaf is exact: F ⊗ – preserves exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the standard linear-algebraic operations transported to the sheaf setting; check exactness on stalks and use local triviality to reduce to the module case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of locally free sheaves and functoriality of Pic (Exercise 13.1.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces and G is a locally free sheaf on Y, then π^* G is a locally free sheaf on X of the same rank; Pic is a contravariant functor from ringed spaces to Ab via pullback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to transport line bundles along morphisms and to compare Picard groups under maps between schemes/analytic spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscheme cut out by a section of a locally free sheaf (Exercise 13.1.I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a section s of a locally free sheaf F on a scheme X, there is a well-defined subscheme V(s) cut out by s = 0; locally under a trivialization s corresponds to functions f_1,...,f_n and V(s) is cut out by these functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is independent of trivialization; an intrinsic construction can be given without coordinates (hint: use Exercise 13.1.I and Exercise 4.5.P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartogs-type extension for locally free sheaves (Exercise 13.1.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a locally Noetherian normal scheme, sections of a locally free sheaf defined away from a closed set of codimension at least 2 extend across that set (algebraic Hartogs phenomenon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for extending rational sections to regular ones in codimension 1 situations; proof uses normality and Noetherianness (Theorem 11.3.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity criterion for rational sections of invertible sheaves (Exercise 13.1.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s is a nonzero rational section of an invertible sheaf on a locally Noetherian normal scheme and s has no poles, then s is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct application of Hartogs-type extension and Exercise 12.5.H; used often to identify global sections from rational data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractional ideals ↔ invertible sheaves and Picard ≅ class group for Dedekind domains (Exercise 13.1.M)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal of the ring of integers O_K in a number field gives an invertible sheaf on Spec O_K; two fractional ideals differing by a principal ideal give the same invertible sheaf; the class group (fractional ideals modulo principal) is isomorphic to Pic( O_K ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies classical ideal class theory with line bundle theory on Dedekind schemes; useful arithmetic example linking algebraic geometry and number theory.
